Court Delivered The Following:
 Order
1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 07.06.2019 passed by the Xxi Additional Small
Causes Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal') in Mvc
No.5392/2018
, the petitioners therein have preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 03.08.2018 at about 11.30 p.m., near Kapile hatti village,
Chitradurga, the deceased was traveling in a Tata ACE vehicle bearing registration No.KA-26/A-5414, at that time, a lorry bearing registration No.KA01-AF-7146, being driven in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the Tata ACE vehicle, due to which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are his children and petitioner No.4 is his mother.
The respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending lorry.

Hence, petitioners preferred MVC No.5392/2018.
4.

Based on the pleadings and the evidence let in, the Tribunal concluded that the accident happened due to rash and negligent riding of the lorry, which was duly insured with respondent No.2 - Insurance company and the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.19,60,000/- to the petitioners.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners have preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the accident is of the year 2018.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has taken his monthly income at Rs.10,000/-.
The same in my opinion is on the lower side.

As per the chart prepared by the Lok-Adalath, the notional income to be taken for the year 2018 is Rs.12,500/-
per month.
The deceased was aged about 38 years at the time of the accident.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121], a multiplier of '15' has to be adopted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the law down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% needs to be added to his future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Given the number of dependants, 1/4th of income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, on the count of loss of dependency, petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.23,62,500/- (12,500 x 12 x 15+40% x 3/4).

6. Further, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644], there are four dependants and they are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium and Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co.,
Ltd Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780, the compensation under these heads also needs to be increased by 10% after every three years.

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss of consortium' and 'loss of estate and funeral expenses', to be increased by 10%, which comes to Rs.1,76,000/- and Rs.33,000/- respectively.
Thus, in all, they are entitled to a sum of Rs.25,71,500/- as against Rs.19,60,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

7. Hence, the following:-
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The total compensation awarded by the  Tribunal is modified and enhanced to Rs.25,71,500/- as against Rs.19,60,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till its realization.

iii. The petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.6,11,500/- over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till its realization.
iv. Respondent No.2 shall pay the said amount to the petitioners within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.

In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has taken his monthly income at Rs.10,000/-.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121], a multiplier of '15' has to be adopted.

6. Further, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
